facts.fact: Minister Léon Juste Ibombo announced at a FASUCE extraordinary session that the government will release US$9 million to build 186 basic telecom sites in rural areas.
The government invested about 4 billion FCFA (US$6.5 million) between 2021 and 2023 to connect 150 white zones and 19 schools to the internet, per Agence Ecofin.

facts.fact: Tribune Eco reports 76 rural 2G sites were deployed under the Fasuce universal service project, and on 19 November 2024 MTN Congo and the World Bank-financed PATN signed a contract of over 1 billion FCFA to upgrade them to 3G.
The universal access fund FASUCE, operational since 2020, has connected over 33,000 citizens in more than 173 localities and installed 183 mobile network sites, the Treasury sheet says.
Congo launched the World Bank-financed PATN in 2023 ($100 million), aimed at broadband access for underserved populations.
